scope: Read-only reaction-scope decisions for Chemistry 1.25 integration; no teaching completion or exam-readiness promotion
interpretation: Required named cases identify source-prescribed chemistry/test contexts, not a claim that each identity explicitly commands a separately memorised equation. Representative cases are suitable editorial choices, not extra specification clauses. Equations are school models with stated limits. No experimental validation.

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Cold water; shared family products. Metal phase can change during reaction; (s) describes initial sample. Group heading names these three.

requiredNamedCases: Li/Na/K reactions with air and water
representativeCases: Reuse 2.1 water equations; compare observed tarnishing in air
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Air contains oxygen and moisture; do not impose M2O on every surface film. No unique air-product equation prescribed. Matched conditions needed for rate inference.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Lithium to sodium to potassium ordering

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Prediction from Group 1 trend, not separate prescribed rubidium/caesium reaction list or exact rate.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Directional reactivity prediction from periodic position
Limits of numerical and physical-property predictions

representativeCases: M → M+ + e−; Na → Na+ + e−
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Configuration explanation of 2.1–2.3; half-equation support, not separately named reaction. C-only explanation does not make water reactions C-only.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Easier electron loss linked to increased reactivity

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Physical colours/states/trends Cl2, Br2, I2; diatomic formula knowledge and phase change, not new reaction.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Physical-property trend distinguished from chemical reactivity

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Predict halogen properties; no separate compulsory chemical case.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Use transition data at a specified pressure
Limits of exact-value and appearance extrapolation

requiredNamedCases: Displacements among chlorine/bromine/iodine and their halides (named group scope)
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Aqueous comparisons; ions aq, halogens supplied as aqueous solutions in these tests. Do not blindly assign pure-element room states to dissolved species. Reverse/self cases no displacement. Na/K spectator choices not separately prescribed salts.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Elemental molecules, halide ions and spectators distinguished
Negative pair outcomes without colourless/no-reaction overclaim
Balanced complete/ionic equations and electron transfer
Ranking inferred from supplied displacement evidence
Matched observations, solvent identity and dilution/reagent limits

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Electronic explanation; reuse 2.7. No extra named reaction requirement.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Seven outer electrons and named configurations
Gain one electron per atom and balanced molecular half-equation
Additional shells, distance and shielding despite greater nuclear charge
Causal reactivity decrease distinguished from Group1 electron loss

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Dry-air composition physical percentages, no reaction.

requiredNamedCases: Metal AND non-metal oxygen-removal methods; iron and phosphorus explicitly examples
representativeCases: Moist iron consumes O2 to rust
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Excess suitable reagent, closed whole gas volume, cooling/comparable pressure and temperature, product leaves measured gas phase. Rust has variable hydration: no invented exact Fe/O2/H2O equation. P2O5 empirical form requires rebalancing. Iron/phosphorus are not exclusive mandated species.
Ignition suitable supervised context. H2O(g) hot, liquid after cooling. S8 + 8O2 → 8SO2 if molecular sulfur supplied. Mg in air can also react with N2; intended oxygen equation explicit.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Sulfur oxide identity and gas phase
Balanced sulfur equation and product comparison

representativeCases: Suitable metal carbonate → metal oxide + CO2
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Heat condition; CuCO3 school model versus explicitly supplied basic carbonate. Not all carbonates decompose under identical heating. Basic-carbonate variant is supporting explanation, not extra named requirement.
Greenhouse effect/climate mechanism, not equation requirement.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Increased carbon dioxide alters energy balance
Not all radiation, not ozone depletion or heat creation

requiredNamedCases: Oxygen-percentage practical with a metal OR a non-metal
representativeCases: Reuse moist iron or phosphorus removal from 2.10
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: One suitable route in practical statement; do not turn OR into AND or demand new equation.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Excess moist iron and airtight endpoint plan

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Water and dilute HCl OR H2SO4 ranking. Ca(OH)2 can be solid suspension plus dissolved portion; Mg steam oxide versus slow cold-water hydroxide. Copper no H2 with these dilute non-oxidising acids. Passivation/sulfate coating and unequal conditions limit rate-ranking. Not every metal × reagent combination separately required.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Fair comparisons, passivation and negative-evidence limits

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Both metal/oxide and metal/aqueous salt families. Suitable initiation for solids; aqueous solvent reactions invalidate simplistic universal series tests. Species are representative, not prescribed exhaustive pairs.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Product evidence, ionic equation and spectators

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Required 11-metal order K Na Li Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Cu Ag Au supports reactions; no new equation for each metal. Hydrogen/carbon are useful references, not extra metals in this list.

representativeCases: Iron + oxygen + water → hydrated iron oxide (word model)
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Both water and oxygen needed; variable rust composition precludes a uniquely mandated balanced hydrated formula. Salt accelerates, not mandatory reactant.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Matched exclusion controls and evidence limits

requiredNamedCases: Barrier methods, galvanising and sacrificial protection of iron
representativeCases: Zn(s) → Zn2+(aq) + 2e−; Mg(s) → Mg2+(aq) + 2e− as sacrifice example
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Barrier is not a new chemical reaction. Galvanising specifies zinc; alternative sacrifice metal is representative. Electrical contact and wet circuit needed; no nearby detached-metal protection.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Sacrificial electron transfer and connected metal

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Oxygen and electron definitions, both agents; representative examples may be reused. Heat for CuO/H2; water phase contextual. Agent is reactant species, not spectator/product.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Paired redox changes and balanced halves
Oxidizing agent accepts electrons and is reduced
Reducing agent donates electrons and is oxidized
Agent oxygen-transfer roles and actual reacting species

requiredNamedCases: Dilute HCl AND dilute H2SO4 with metals; Mg/Zn/Fe are publisher examples
representativeCases: For M = Mg, Zn, Fe: M(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MCl2(aq) + H2(g)
For M = Mg, Zn, Fe: M(s) + H2SO4(aq) → MSO4(aq) + H2(g)
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: These six suitable representative combinations cover both acids; not exclusive publisher-permitted metals or six separately mandated named cases. FeII salts; no unsafe extrapolation to alkali-metal acid tests. Hydrogen identification separate from effervescence.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Publisher example metals and both named dilute acids
Rate versus final amount and limiting reactant
Repeatability, collection losses and evidence limits

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Ores versus native elements; no extra extraction equation.

Unreactive native metals as a tendency

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Heated iron reduction; iron phase depends actual process stage, do not universalise (s). Al school half-equation in molten cryolite/alumina bath, metal liquid in industrial cell; ions molten electrolyte not aqueous. Detailed furnace/anode sequence not prescribed by this identity.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Carbon position and suitable oxide reduction
Mobile ions, cathode electron gain and carbon anode role

representativeCases: Use supplied extraction equation/process and check balance/relative reactivity
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Detailed specific industrial extraction processes explicitly not required. Do not create a compulsory bank entry for each metal or furnace step.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Interpret starting material and method from information
Ore grade, theoretical yield and recovery calculation
Evidence-based energy/waste trade-offs and missing data

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Al/Cu/Fe/steel uses and properties. Oxide/passive-film context not demand for separate oxidation equations. Steel limited mild, high-carbon, stainless.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Aluminium low density and alloy strength use
Aluminium heat transfer, forming and oxide protection
Copper electrical conductivity and ductility for wire
Iron magnetic behaviour and steel distinctions
Mild-steel formability and high-carbon hardness trade-off

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Alloy mixture, variable proportions; do not invent compound formation equation.

Variable composition distinguished from fixed compound formula

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Hardness structural model, no reaction.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Regular pure-metal arrangement and plastic movement

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Litmus/phenolphthalein/methyl-orange colours; indicator equilibrium equations not prescribed.
School pH scale classification; no extra equation.

Solution pH distinguished from acid ionization strength

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Universal indicator approximate pH; no extra equation.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Compare universal indicator with formulation chart

representativeCases: Aqueous acids supply H+; aqueous alkalis supply OH−
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Aqueous dissociation/species skill; no separately prescribed named ionisation equation. H+ school shorthand; ammonia is not a hydroxide formula.
Full neutralisation stoichiometry. Endpoint not automatically equivalence/pH7; named acid/base pairs representative.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Alkali neutralizes acid and net ionic equation

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Titration method; no additional exclusive acid/base pair. Aqueous solutions, appropriate indicator, delivered volumes and balanced stoichiometry.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Pipette/filler, burette, flask and appropriate rinses
Indicator, white tile, tip and initial reading
Swirling, dropwise addition and lasting endpoint
Rough run, concordance and justified mean

representativeCases: Ag+(aq) + Cl−(aq) → AgCl(s) is illustrative use of solubility
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: All six solubility rules and exceptions required, not infinite salt-pair reactions. All nitrates/common Na K NH4 salts soluble; chlorides except Ag/PbII; sulfates except Ba/Ca/PbII; carbonates except Na/K/NH4; hydroxides except Na/K/Ca (Ca slightly soluble).
editorialRequirementSummaries: Sodium, potassium, ammonium and nitrate rules
Hydroxide exceptions and slightly soluble calcium
Finite solubility and full ion-pair classification

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Proton-transfer principle; examples not separately prescribed. Reversible weak-base aqueous equilibrium distinct from complete neutralisation.
No new reaction; roles assigned within particular equation.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Ammonia example conserves atoms and charge

requiredNamedCases: HCl, H2SO4, HNO3 reaction families with metals, bases and metal carbonates; nitric-acid/metal reactions excluded
representativeCases: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2; Mg + H2SO4 → MgSO4 + H2
CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O; CuO + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O; CuO + 2HNO3 → Cu(NO3)2 + H2O
Mg(OH)2 + 2HCl → MgCl2 + 2H2O; Mg(OH)2 + H2SO4 → MgSO4 + 2H2O; Mg(OH)2 + 2HNO3 → Mg(NO3)2 + 2H2O
NH3 + HCl → NH4Cl; 2NH3 + H2SO4 → (NH4)2SO4; NH3 + HNO3 → NH4NO3
CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2; MgCO3 + H2SO4 → MgSO4 + H2O + CO2; MgCO3 + 2HNO3 → Mg(NO3)2 + H2O + CO2
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Representative coverage grid, not every possible metal/base/carbonate. Dilute aqueous acids; suitable solids/aqueous bases, soluble salt aq, H2/CO2 gas, water liquid. Nitric acid + metals explicitly outside this scope. Ammonia gives no additional water. Insoluble sulfate coating can arrest some carbonate/metal reactions.
editorialRequirementSummaries: HCl/H₂SO₄ metal salt and hydrogen with conditions
Oxide/hydroxide reactions with all three acids
Carbonate salt/water/CO₂ with all three acids
Salt anion and metal charge with balanced examples

requiredNamedCases: Metal oxides, metal hydroxides and ammonia as bases
representativeCases: Reuse oxide/hydroxide/ammonia equations in 2.37; NH3 + H+ → NH4+
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Alkali is water-soluble base. No requirement that all bases are soluble or have OH in formula.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Oxides, hydroxides and ammonia as bases
Ammonia proton acceptance and aqueous alkalinity

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Insoluble reactant to soluble salt: excess solid then filter/concentrate/cool/dry. Choice representative, shared with named 2.42; no unique new salt demanded.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Excess solid and adequate mixing/reaction time

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Acid/alkali soluble-salt preparation; titration then uncontaminated measured repeat. Salt representative, not exclusively NaCl.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Use titration because soluble excess cannot be filtered

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Two soluble reagents yield insoluble salt; precipitate/filter/wash/dry. Examples not new exclusive required salts; named lead case separately 2.43C.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Two soluble ion sources for insoluble target

requiredNamedCases: Pure dry hydrated CuSO4 crystals starting CuO
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Warm dilute acid; excess insoluble oxide removed. Crystallisation gives CuSO4·5H2O(s) in school case; dry surface does not mean anhydrous. Separate hydration bookkeeping optional, not pretend crystal formula is aqueous product. Applies both papers.
editorialRequirementSummaries: CuO and sulfuric acid with excess/controlled warming
Separate and dry hydrated crystals gently
Purity, losses and supervised practical limits

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Named product prescribed; nitrate/sodium-sulfate reagent choice representative soluble pair. Filter, wash, dry under supervised procedure; not direct heating acid/lead chemicals.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Toxicity, lead waste and identity/purity limits

requiredNamedCases: Tests for H2, O2, CO2, NH3 and Cl2
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Named tests required; not five new compulsory equations. H2 lighted splint pop; O2 glowing splint relights; CO2 limewater cloudy; NH3 damp red litmus blue; Cl2 damp litmus bleached. Splint fuel unspecified, no unique O2 splint equation; indicator/bleaching mechanism equations optional. Water moisture essential for papers.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Hydrogen lighted-splint pop versus oxygen glowing-splint relight
Ammonia damp red litmus turns blue
Test conditions, sequence and inference limits

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Flame-test procedure; clean wire and avoid sodium contamination. No combustion equation for each salt.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Clean loop or approved alternative and blank check
Sample in non-luminous flame and record colour

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Li/Na/K/Ca/Cu flame colours are excitation/emission evidence, not distinct reaction equations.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Cation result does not identify anion or purity

requiredNamedCases: NH4+ with NaOH and identify gas
Cu2+, Fe2+, Fe3+ with NaOH solution
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Warm ammonium mixture; NH3 damp red litmus blue. Hydroxides blue/green/brown precipitates; salts supplying cations need not be individually enumerated. OH− aqueous, precipitate solid; distinguish FeII/III.
editorialRequirementSummaries: NH₄⁺ plus NaOH and warming gives identified ammonia
Gas test kept separate from alkaline liquid
Cu²⁺ blue, Fe²⁺ green and Fe³⁺ brown precipitates
Precipitate versus solution and Fe²⁺ oxidation sequence
Balanced hydroxide/ammonium examples and inference limits

requiredNamedCases: CO3^2− with HCl and gas test
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Halides acidify dilute HNO3 (never HCl), white/cream/yellow precipitates; sulfate acidify dilute HCl then BaCl2 (not H2SO4), white. Carbonate can be insoluble solid; net CO3 ion form is bookkeeping, do not mark all carbonate samples aq. Use suitable actual carbonate molecular example if states demanded. CO2 limewater secondary test.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Dilute nitric acid then silver nitrate halide test
Chloride white, bromide cream, iodide yellow precipitates
Avoid introduced chloride and carbonate interference
Acidified barium chloride white sulfate precipitate
Avoid introduced sulfate and carbonate interference
Carbonate hydrochloric acid release and limewater gas evidence
Separate portions and balanced charge/atom examples

representativeCases: CuSO4(s) + 5H2O(l) → CuSO4·5H2O(s) as simplified hydration model
decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: White to blue; test establishes water presence, not purity. Equation supports named chemical change but exact hydrate stoichiometry not separately demanded by 2.49. Excess liquid/sample may dissolve salt.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Fresh white anhydrous CuSO₄ turns blue with water
Moisture contamination and presence versus purity

decisions.statesConditionsAndScopeLimits: Physical purity test water by boiling/freezing point at stated pressure. No new reaction; 100 °C/0 °C school values at standard atmospheric pressure.
editorialRequirementSummaries: Phase-change temperature with correct pure-water reference
Physical purity versus chemical water-presence evidence
